Add the `types/` folder of the resource to your editor's Lua language server library to get these types.

## PMMSkillData

The data of one skill of a character, as returned by `GetSkillDataClient` / `GetSkillDataServer`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lvl` | `number` | yes | Current level (0 if never trained) |
| `exp` | `number` | yes | Current EXP in the skill |
| `perks` | `table<string, boolean>` | no | Unlocked perks, keyed by perk id as a string (e.g. `"3"`) |
| `choices` | `table<string, string>` | no | Choices made on perks that have `choices` in the config, keyed by perk id |

## PMMSkillDefinition

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | yes | Name shown in the book and in the menus |
| `points` | `table<number, PMMSkillPoint>` | yes | One entry per level (1, 2, 3, ...) |
| `levels` | `table<number, number>` | no | EXP needed for each level. If omitted it is computed with Config.ExpFunction |
| `hidden` | `boolean` | no | Secret skill: no page in the book and no EXP notifications until level 1 |
| `reveal` | `{ title: string, description: string }` | no | Notification shown when a hidden skill reaches level 1 |

## PMMSkillPoint

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |
| `description` | `string` | yes |  |
| `perk` | `number` | no | Perk id (= the level). Perks are unlocked at an instructor and cost a perk point |
| `choices` | `table<string, string>` | no | Perk with a choice: key saved in the DB -> button label at the instructor. Read it with exports.pmm_skill_system:GetSkillPerkChoice |
